ACTION: Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-skills/references/flowcharts.md (the skill requires this before adding a flowchart: when one earns its place, graphviz style rules, render tool)

ACTION: Read specs/cache-invalidation-baseline.md (the saved reasons from the 11 of 15 runs that purged a key that should have expired, so the decision nodes use the predicates agents actually misjudged)

ACTION: Read skills/cache-invalidation/SKILL.md (to see the current purge-vs-expire guidance, match its style, and decide where the flowchart goes)

I'm starting with three reads. I haven't written the flowchart yet because its decision nodes need to come from the baseline reasons, not from my guess at why agents purge.

Once I've read them, I'll add a small flowchart to `skills/cache-invalidation/SKILL.md`. The branch points will be observable conditions, such as whether stale data is harmful or whether the TTL will lapse soon enough. They won't be soft guidance like "prefer expiry". I'll also check whether the baseline reasons show agents knowingly overriding a rule under pressure. If they do, a rationalization table might be needed in addition to the flowchart.

After the edit I'll re-run the same three scenarios, 5 reps each, with the flowchart in place. That shows whether the 11 of 15 purge errors actually drop. I'll report the new count whether or not it improves.
